races.name: Zyn Frontrunner EBF Restricted Novice Stakes (For Horses In Bands B, C And D) (EBF Restricted Race Qualifier) (GBB Race)
Zyn Strong Stride EBF Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Date Line
runners_data.note: Unbeaten in a win and placed at 7f on Good ground at Newmarket and Goodwood, making this step to a mile on identical conditions a logical progression; Charlie Johnston sends her back after a 420-day layoff — the fitness query is real but the 2/2 record on fast turf and uncontested lead gives her every structural advantage, and Callum Shepherd's light touch suits a front-runner dictating her own fractions.

runners_data.name: Evening Call
runners_data.note: A William Haggas newcomer or lightly raced type with no public form to assess, so running style is genuinely unknown; she sits at the rear in this mapping not because she is a natural hold-up horse but because there is simply no room for another prominent runner in a three-horse field with Date Line already committed to the lead, making her actual tactical position on the day the critical unknown.

runners_data.name: Gilding The Lily
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin partners this Gosden filly who ran a solid second at 7f on Sandown's flat track 14 days ago, suggesting she arrives race-fit and in a rhythm; she is a natural prominent racer who should slot neatly into second behind Date Line, and the drop to a still-competitive 1m on Good to Firm ground is unlikely to inconvenience her, though she needs Date Line to tie up to reverse what looks a clear pace hierarchy.

races.paceDynamic: Date Line is the sole confirmed front-runner in a field of three and will lead from the outset, setting a measured, uncontested gallop on Good to Firm ground over Newmarket's straight mile. Gilding The Lily will likely track in second from a prominent position, with Evening Call — a lightly raced type whose natural style is uncertain — sitting at the rear by default in what amounts to a single-file procession. With no rival to pressure Date Line, she controls every element of pace: she can conserve energy early and dictate exactly when the race quickens, which is a significant structural advantage. This race shape strongly favours the front-running profile — an uncontested, self-regulated leader on fast ground over a flat mile is a textbook setup for a wire-to-wire performance, and any horse needing a true run to come from is compromised by the lack of genuine pace to chase.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Date Line Controls Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Date Line leads throughout at a self-selected tempo and quickens clear in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Date Line, uncontested on the front end, can regulate fractions to suit herself and deploy her finishing kick from a position of dominance; her 2/2 record on similar going underpins that confidence in conditions.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Gilding The Lily tracks Date Line closely enough to respond when the leader kicks and gets first run.
scenarios.body: Gilding The Lily, stepping back in trip from her Sandown second, pressing from second position could outsprint the leader in the final furlong if Date Line has overextended herself; the Gosden yard's fresh runners often run creditably at this stage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closer Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely slow early, creating a sprint finish that Evening Call can produce a sharp late effort into.
scenarios.body: Evening Call, placed at the rear by redistribution rather than true hold-up instinct, would need the race to collapse into a late dash and a significant step forward on debut form to factor; the William Haggas yard can produce well-prepared debutants, but the scenario relies on pace dynamics not reflecting her likely natural positioning.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Upset From Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If Date Line is uncharacteristically slow into stride or suffers interference, scrambling the expected shape.
scenarios.body: With a 420-day absence, Date Line carries a residual question mark about readiness at the break, and any hesitation could compress the field and open a chaotic finish; in that scenario Gilding The Lily, with the benefit of a recent run 14 days ago, is best placed to capitalise.

watchPoints.text: Watch Date Line's break from the stalls — after a 420-day absence, any sluggishness at the off could compromise her front-running position and alter the entire race shape.

Watch whether Gilding The Lily presses Date Line aggressively or allows a gap — if Gilding The Lily sits tight to the leader it increases pressure on Date Line; if she gives ground, it hands Date Line an even freer rein.

Watch Evening Call's early positioning — if her jockey Harry Davies sends her forward, this effectively becomes a race with no genuine hold-up runner, and the shape collapses entirely into a front-runners' affair.

Watch the sectionals in the first three furlongs — on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket, a truly slow early pace from an uncontested Date Line could compress final-furlong margins significantly and flatter any closer finishing late.

Watch the Haggas stable's handling of Evening Call's race fitness — lightly raced Haggas runners on fast ground at Newmarket often arrive spot-on, and any market support could signal she is more forward than her sparse form suggests.

races.name: Maritime Cargo Sts Freight Frenzy Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Sir Edward Lear
runners_data.note: Prominent-style stayer dropping sharply from 12f and 16f trips, and while the step back to 8f is a significant concern, his three sim-going runs show consistent placing and James Owen has placed him thoughtfully; the visor (v headgear) is worn, and 78 days off is notable — he may need the race to warm up.|

runners_data.name: Calyxoh
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning quickly on 12 days' rest, lightly raced at 8f on Good going (four runs), and Dylan Hogan takes over; the stable (Patrick Morris, T14:0/8) is out of form, and Calyxoh's sim-going record (7/15, 1W2P) suggests he is capable without being consistent.|

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Progressive prominent racer in career-best form — back-to-back wins at 8f on Good, the most recent just 13 days ago — and the hat-trick bid is the standout narrative here; Laura Pearson rides and David Loughnane's yard is ticking (T14:1/11), the distance and going are spot on.|

runners_data.name: Special Ghaiyyath
runners_data.note: Has strong finishing speed on paper but is a true hold-up horse whose natural position at the rear is unavailable in this field, meaning it will likely race in midfield against its instincts; four of its last five runs have been disappointing (form 368974) and the STYLE_FIT flag of 0.94 tempers confidence materially.|

runners_data.name: Currumbin
runners_data.note: Exposed stayer stepping down to 8f from 12f–16f trips and has not won in recent starts, with a sim-going record that flatters (9/15) but rarely converts; similarly to Special Ghaiyyath, this is a true hold-up horse whose preferred rear position is compromised by the field composition, and the drop in trip adds a further question mark.|

runners_data.name: Triggerman
runners_data.note: The sole front-runner — Patrick Morris's only pacemaker in this field — and although his form reads 39-680 with no recent wins, an uncontested lead on Good to Firm Newmarket turf over 8f is a genuinely favourable scenario; 22 days since last run is fine, and the apprentice Finlay Bassett (7lb) reduces his weight burden.|

runners_data.name: Rising Force
runners_data.note: The highest-rated horse in the field (OR=74) and a natural hold-up type with genuine 8f form — two placings and a win in his last five at the distance on Good — making him the most credible of the closers even if the pace does not set up perfectly; Marco Ghiani is a strong booking and John Butler's yard is firing (T14:5/22).|

runners_data.name: Mr Ubiquitous
runners_data.note: Prominent racer with strong recent form at 7f on Good but yet to win beyond that trip — this step up to 8f for the first time on the sim-going profile is an open question; Kaiya Fraser takes over and Harry Eustace is lightly active (T14:1/9), though the OR=73 and form 9-1505 suggest he can win off this mark when conditions align.|

races.paceDynamic: Triggerman is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, should bowl along at a comfortable, self-regulated gallop on Good to Firm ground over this flat Newmarket July mile — a setup that rewards those who can track the pace and quicken late rather than those deep in the pack. Sir Edward Lear, The Sweet Escape, and Mr Ubiquitous are all prominent-style horses who will want to sit within two or three lengths of Triggerman, creating a compact, organised early order rather than a hot-speed scenario. Rising Force, Special Ghaiyyath, and Currumbin are genuine hold-up horses, but with Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin redistributed into the midfield map because the field contains more true hold-up types than the pace shape can accommodate at the rear, their chances are somewhat contingent on whether they can find a clear passage from further back than ideal. The field holds more hold-up and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position, and Triggerman, Sir Edward Lear, and The Sweet Escape are most likely to actually dictate the early order; this controlled, single-pace-setter scenario strongly favours prominent racers who can track economically and produce a sustained finish, rather than deep closers needing a searching tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Triggerman Controls, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Triggerman leads at an honest but uncontested gallop and the prominent trio track him into the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Triggerman sets a true but manageable pace, and the horses tucked just behind — Sir Edward Lear, The Sweet Escape, Mr Ubiquitous — enjoy the perfect stalking position to peel off and challenge as the field straightens; on Good to Firm Newmarket turf this controlled shape routinely sees the first-two-from-the-front dominate. Prominent racers with recent 8f form over similar ground hold the structural advantage here, and The Sweet Escape's back-to-back wins at 8f on Good suit this scenario particularly well.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Triggerman Steals It Wire To Wire
scenarios.trigger: If Triggerman is allowed a soft, uncontested lead and no one makes a move until it is too late.
scenarios.body: With a lone front-runner and prominent horses content to settle, Triggerman could exploit the lack of pressure to steal an unassailable break turning for home; handicappers and prominent rivals may collectively underestimate the lead margin until the damage is done. At OR=60 off a 22-day break Triggerman is lightly weighted and Patrick Morris has placed him here — the wire-to-wire outcome is a live threat if the pace is truly pedestrian.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Get Through Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely strong enough to string the field out and leave a gap for closers to thread through.
scenarios.body: Rising Force has the strongest recent form of the hold-up runners (OR=74, second and fifth on identical 8f Good ground) and could pick up the pieces if the midfield gets crowded and prominent horses flatter to deceive; however, Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin are racing out of their natural positions and their chances here are specifically discounted by that redistribution. Rising Force is the one genuine closer whose style fit and form make this scenario credible, but the moderate expected pace makes it a low-probability shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Lead Scrambles Result
scenarios.trigger: If one or more prominent horses push forward unexpectedly to dispute the lead with Triggerman, lifting the tempo.
scenarios.body: Should Sir Edward Lear or Mr Ubiquitous elect to go forward and force Triggerman to work harder, the pace dynamic shifts and both deep closers and staying-types could benefit from a messy, strung-out finish; this is the scenario most likely to throw the race open to a surprise result. Calyxoh, lightly raced over 8f on Good and fresh off a 12-day break, would be the most interesting beneficiary if the race falls apart at the front.

watchPoints.text: Watch Triggerman's early strides — if Finlay Bassett is given any daylight at all, no other runner has the pace profile to challenge for the lead and the solo front-runner advantage becomes structural rather than coincidental.

The Sweet Escape's freshness is the key variable — three wins in her last four and a 13-day turnaround on identical ground; if she travels smoothly in second or third, she is the most dangerous horse in the race at the top of the straight.

Rising Force (OR=74, Marco Ghiani) is being asked to close from further back than ideal against a likely-moderate pace — watch whether Ghiani elects to push forward earlier than usual to avoid being stranded.|

Special Ghaiyyath and Currumbin are both natural hold-up horses forced into midfield by the field's composition; if they are hemmed in and unable to find daylight entering the final two furlongs, their races will be over before they begin.

Mr Ubiquitous is unproven at 8f — all his best form is at 7f on similar ground — so watch whether Kaiya Fraser opts to press forward rather than sit and wait, which would change the tempo and potentially trigger Scenario D.

races.name: Maritime Cargo Sts Container Storage Solutions Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Fifty Nifty
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator with a recent winning run over this course and distance on good ground; trainer Martin Dunne has modest current form (1/4 over 14 days) and the 7-day turnaround is short, but Callum Shepherd rides and the horse's similar-going record (1W2P in 15) gives confidence on the surface.

runners_data.name: Mumayaz
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old hold-up specialist who has run five of his last five over this exact 6f trip on good ground, recording a win and two places; Tony Carroll's yard is in decent form and the 22-day break looks straightforward, with this trip and surface clearly his optimum conditions.

runners_data.name: Ziggy's Condor
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who has placed over 6f on good ground recently; Adam Kirby's yard has been quiet (0/8 in 14 days) but apprentice Shay Farmer (5lb) claims useful weight, and the horse's ability to sit just off the pace makes it a natural beneficiary if the front-runners set a genuine gallop.

runners_data.name: Spirit Of Jenny
runners_data.note: Four-year-old prominent type who has been remarkably consistent in placing positions (0W4P in recent similar-going runs), including two runner-up finishes; trainer Steph Hollinshead has had a quiet 14-day spell and the 8-day turnaround is tight, but Dougie Costello's booking is an upgrade.

runners_data.name: Northcliff
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a visor who has won over 6f on good ground and placed here before; Ross Burdon's yard is running at 0/7 over 14 days, the 13-day break is manageable, and on similar ground his record of 1W3P in 15 runs suggests he handles conditions but needs things to go his way late.

runners_data.name: Beauzon
runners_data.note: Confirmed front-runner who has recently won back-to-back over 6f on standard ground; the two recent wins came at Southwell and his similar-going figures at Newmarket are poor (0W0P in 15 runs), which is a significant flag — his ability to dictate is clear but the Newmarket July course on good-to-firm is not his proven arena.

runners_data.name: Rebel Path
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer wearing a hood with a solid record of placing over 6f on good ground (1W4P in 15); Stuart Williams has had three winners in 14 days (3/31) and Chloe Lyons claims 7lb, providing a substantial weight relief that could offset this horse's need for things to set up perfectly from the rear.

runners_data.name: Romantic Twilight
runners_data.note: Three-year-old front-runner who won over 6f on good ground and has been campaigned exclusively on that surface (1W1P in 10 similar-going runs); William Stone's yard is quiet (0/6) and the 23-day break is unremarkable, but this juvenile is the most natural pace-setter in the field and will press hard from the off.

runners_data.name: Currahee
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams's second string, wearing a tongue-strap and hood combination; a prominent racer who won over 7f on standard and has placed over 6f on good ground (1W1P in 13 runs), but a recent run of 4th at this trip and the 14-day return to course makes this one to watch rather than lead the market.

runners_data.name: Bayraat
runners_data.note: A ten-year-old with a fine recent record of placed finishes over 6f on good ground (1W6P in 15 runs, including four consecutive 2nds); Tom Tate has had no runners in 14 days and this horse is a natural hold-up type whose true running style is at the back of the field — shown in midfield on the map only because the field is structurally overcrowded with closers.

runners_data.name: Molly Mac
runners_data.note: Three-year-old prominent racer who won over 6f on good ground on her most recent start; Micky Fenton's yard has had two winners in three runners over 14 days, and Grace McEntee's booking on a lightly-raced filly with a clear form line on this surface makes her interesting at a competitive weight.

runners_data.name: Em Jay Kay
runners_data.note: A seven-year-old hold-up type carrying a hood whose natural position is off the pace; Phil McEntee has had no runners in 14 days and the 31-day break is the longest in the field — the horse runs off a career-low OR of 55 and finished last when returning from a break previously, so the fitness question is real, and being pushed into mapped midfield understates how far back he will likely race.

races.paceDynamic: Romantic Twilight and Beauzon are the two confirmed front-runners in a 12-runner 6f handicap on good-to-firm ground at Newmarket's July course, and with both likely to press for the early lead, the pace should be honest rather than suicidal — a competitive but sustainable gallop that keeps the race truly run from the off. Ziggy's Condor and Spirit Of Jenny will look to track the pace prominently, adding further pressure to the early stages and ensuring no runner can afford to switch off. The honest pace on a flat, galloping track that typically rewards those who can travel into the race and sustain their effort through the final two furlongs means this shape primarily favours prominent racers or strong-finishing hold-up horses who have genuine late acceleration — not those forced out of position. Bayraat and Em Jay Kay are genuine hold-up types who cannot all secure their natural position at the rear of this competitive field; Beauzon, with its stronger recent front-running profile, is most likely to dictate, while Romantic Twilight will push from the inside, and the redistribution of Bayraat and Em Jay Kay into mapped midfield positions reflects the structural overcrowding at the back of the field rather than their true racing style.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Contested Lead, Prominent Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If Romantic Twilight and Beauzon push each other to an honest gallop and a prominent tracker sustains the pressure to the line.
scenarios.body: The pace set by the two leaders creates a true-run race on a galloping track, and a horse sitting a length or two off the pace throughout is perfectly positioned to pounce in the final furlong without burning energy early.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Pinches It
scenarios.trigger: If Beauzon or Romantic Twilight steals a decisive break and the field fails to close the gap in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: One leader edges clear by settling into a rhythm that the field cannot disrupt, and the good-to-firm ground rewards the horse in front who doesn't have to decelerate through the closing stages.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Closers Sweep Through
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace between Romantic Twilight and Beauzon burns both out, opening the door for hold-up horses finishing strongly.
scenarios.body: A genuinely hard-run early gallop sees both leaders tied up inside the final furlong, and horses held off the pace with natural acceleration pick through the field on the outside.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Grind, Lower Weights Land
scenarios.trigger: If the race settles into a uniform gallop and the weight advantage of the lower-rated runners proves decisive in a grinding finish.
scenarios.body: Without a truly punishing pace, the race develops into a sustained test of stamina over the final two furlongs, and the lighter-weighted, fresher handicappers grind past tiring rivals.

watchPoints.text: Beauzon's front-running profile is straightforward but his course record at Newmarket on good-to-firm is 0W0P from 15 runs — if Romantic Twilight pushes him hard early on uncongenial ground, he could capitulate inside the final furlong.

Em Jay Kay returns after 31 days for Phil McEntee's yard with no recent runners in 14 days — monitor market move carefully as this horse has form questions at this trip on turf and comes from a position of fitness uncertainty.

Ziggy's Condor is ridden by 5lb claimer Shay Farmer for a trainer (Adam Kirby) who has had no winners in 14 days — if the horse gets a prominent pitch behind the leaders and is given a positive ride, the weight allowance could prove significant in a close finish.

Rebel Path's 7lb claim from Chloe Lyons is the largest weight relief in the field — in a race where the pace map forces several hold-up horses into positions they may not naturally take, this horse's genuine late-running profile could see it finishing faster than the map suggests if the gallop is truly honest.

Bayraat and Em Jay Kay are both genuine hold-up types mapped to midfield positions due to structural overcrowding at the rear — watch where they actually settle in the early stages, as neither horse is likely to race where the map places them and their finishing positions will depend entirely on whether the pace generates the gaps they need.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: God Of War
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist for Tom Clover with Marco Ghiani aboard; 100 days off the track is the key query but has winning and placed form on Good ground, and a return to 1m suits the profile of a horse finishing from the rear.

runners_data.name: Sterling Knight
runners_data.note: Toby Moore claims 7lb for the seven-year-old Ed Dunlop runner who is race-fit at 13 days; prominent style is his trademark on this course and distance, and his strong 1m Good-ground record (sim-going 1W4P) keeps him firmly in contention.

runners_data.name: Principality
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's four-year-old won at this trip on Good last time out and Harry Fraser rides; 70 days off is a consideration, but the horse holds-up and has the tactical profile to benefit from the race shape here, with a clean run critical.

runners_data.name: Zarathos
runners_data.note: Callum Shepherd partners a well-credentialed hold-up type for Dylan Cunha who is in fair form (4-1-1 recent sim-going record); 2 wins from 11 on similar going and proven over 1m, though the step up from 7f needs confirming at this level.

runners_data.name: Croupier
runners_data.note: Robert Havlin rides the seven-year-old who is naturally a prominent racer, but with four rivals competing for those front slots, he is expected to settle deeper than he would prefer — the STYLE_FIT flag (0.92) tempers confidence in any scenario that requires him to stride forward.

runners_data.name: Brocklesby Bill
runners_data.note: The race's lone front-runner for Kathy Turner and Charlie Tucker (7lb claim); has won twice and placed twice in five similar-going starts, and his hold on the lead is essentially unchallenged — the headgear (h) and only 16 days between runs suggests freshness and willingness to bowl along.

runners_data.name: Mythical Guest
runners_data.note: George Margarson's six-year-old is a genuine hold-up horse but is mapped to midfield due to redistribution pressure; Mason Paetel (5lb) rides a horse with zero wins from 11 similar-going starts, so despite the positional context, the form record on Good ground is weak.

runners_data.name: Storm Star
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's five-year-old carries top weight (142lbs) and is prominent by style, but has only 4 similar-going runs from 15 and no wins on like ground — Alfie Redman (7lb) rides, and 57 days off adds a fitness doubt, making the high weight a real concern.

runners_data.name: Hickory
runners_data.note: Jamie Osborne's eight-year-old carries joint-top weight but has proven course-and-distance winning form on Good ground (sim-going 2W5P from 12 starts), and the headgear (p) is unchanged; William Carver rides and the prominent style suits this race shape if he can avoid the positional scramble.

runners_data.name: Tuscan Hills
runners_data.note: Rob Hornby partners the Nigel Tinkler four-year-old who is race-fit at 13 days but has a limited record at this trip, with form mainly over further or shorter; recent form figures of 0-0-5-5 suggest he is struggling to land a blow, and the prominent style may see him embroiled in the congestion battle.

races.paceDynamic: Brocklesby Bill is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with only a 3yo headgear-wearing sort facing a single dedicated pace-setter, he should slot into an uncontested lead at a fair but manageable gallop on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course. Behind him, Storm Star, Sterling Knight, Hickory, and Tuscan Hills all want prominent positions, creating a congested group of four chasing two realistic slots in the first three, meaning early shuffling and potential traffic friction from the 3f pole home. Croupier is a natural prominent racer who is unlikely to secure that berth given the competition for position, and will likely find himself racing further back than ideal. This race shape — a genuine but not brutal pace set by a single front-runner with a congested prominent pack — strongly favours hold-up horses with class and a turn of foot, giving the trailing closers a clean target to aim at off a true gallop; horses who can travel wide and finish through traffic stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Brocklesby Bill Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill leads uncontested at a steady-to-fair clip and the prominent pack wastes energy fighting for position.
scenarios.body: Brocklesby Bill sets a comfortable fractions under Charlie Tucker, the prominent quartet neutralise each other, and the race sets up perfectly for a hold-up finisher to sprint past a tiring wall.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If the congested prominent group settles quickly and one emerges to press Brocklesby Bill, quickening off a stronger pace.
scenarios.body: A genuine contest develops between two or three prominent horses from 2f out, rewarding whoever has tracked widest and freshest; a well-handicapped prominent type who avoids the scrimmage earns a winning position.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Caught In Traffic
scenarios.trigger: If the hold-up horses get boxed in on the rail as the prominent group fans wide and the pace collapses entering the final furlong.
scenarios.body: The prominent horses control the tempo and the finish, leaving the closers with no room to accelerate at the critical moment; a prominent racer with a clean passage wins as the field bunches.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Brocklesby Bill goes too fast early and the field strings out, leaving a clear gap for hold-up horses to sprint through.
scenarios.body: A fast early pace burns off the prominent pack and the closers who have settled deepest get a clear run on the outside in the final 2f; those with the highest top speed on good ground finish best.

watchPoints.text: Prominent congestion is severe — Storm Star, Sterling Knight, Hickory, and Tuscan Hills all want the same two berths directly behind Brocklesby Bill, and interference between the 6f and 3f poles is a near-certainty.

Brocklesby Bill's unchallenged lead means the race tempo is entirely in his hands — if Charlie Tucker allows the pace to drop significantly, hold-up horses like God Of War and Principality will face a test of speed rather than stamina.

Croupier's inability to secure his natural prominent slot means Robert Havlin must quickly decide whether to push forward aggressively (risking burning energy) or settle mid-to-rear — either way, the horse is unlikely to race in its most productive position.

God Of War is 100 days absent and steps up from 7f to 1m — connections will need a near-perfect run from the rear, and any traffic trouble at the 2f-3f bottleneck could end his chance before it begins.
Mythical Guest has zero wins from 11 starts on similar going — even if Mason Paetel (5lb) finds a clear run, the raw form makes a winning performance on this surface exceptional rather than expected.

races.name: Racing Welfare Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rogue Empire
runners_data.note: Two wins from four starts over 2m on Good ground make him the clear form pick at this trip; redistributed to the lead as the only horse likely to set the pace, though this is out of his natural hold-up role — a STYLE_FIT of 0.80 means discount him if the race requires him to make the running against his instincts, but his recent 2m winning sequence on similar going is the single most relevant piece of form in the race.

runners_data.name: Tarbat Ness
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old with a win and three places from six runs on similar going, including a win over 17f on Good; natural hold-up horse who should find a clear route around the outside in a small field, and his course-distance profile is solid enough to make him a genuine placed threat.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Consistent placer with five runs all resulting in a top-three finish over 2m on Good or Standard going; his true style is a deep closer but the map places him in midfield due to the crowded hold-up group — the honest read is that he will likely be towards the rear and needs a well-run race to finish his effort.

runners_data.name: Mio Amico
runners_data.note: 94 days off the track is the biggest flag here, and his form over this trip is mainly on Standard ground with no recent Good-ground runs to reference; a natural hold-up horse shown in midfield on the map, his real position will be further back, and fitness on return from a lengthy layoff is an open question.

runners_data.name: Laravie
runners_data.note: Wears the visor for the first time and has a strong recent profile — four wins and places over 2m on Good ground — with trainer James Owen in sharp form (9/45 in 14 days); her hold-up style is her natural game and the map pushes her into midfield, but in a small, strung-out field she is capable of making her move early enough to be competitive.

runners_data.name: Free World
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, which is a meaningful concern in a 2m contest on fast ground; has won over 2m on Good ground but most of her recent form is over shorter, and her true hold-up style means she will need a strong pace to close into — absent that, the finishing-fade flag is a real negative.

runners_data.name: The Craftymaster
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins including over 2m on Good ground give him solid recent credentials, and the tongue-tie has been worn in his winning runs; naturally a hold-up horse placed into midfield on the map, his lower OR of 57 leaves him well handicapped if reproducing form, and Mason Paetel (5lb claim via Myla Coppins) reduces his weight burden further.

races.paceDynamic: Rogue Empire is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner 2m handicap on Good to Firm ground at Newmarket's July course, and with no genuine rival to press him from the off, he is set to control proceedings at a measured, sustainable gallop that suits a horse with two recent wins over this trip. The remainder of the field — An Bradan Feasa, Mio Amico, Laravie, Free World, and The Craftymaster — are all natural hold-up types redistributed into midfield positions on the map because the rear of the race is overcrowded with closers; Tarbat Ness adds further weight to the hold-up cluster. With one genuine pace-setter dictating an uncontested rhythm over two miles on a flat, galloping track, the race shape strongly favours horses who can travel close enough to the tempo to launch a clean, sustained run from two furlongs out — the true deep closers risk being caught in traffic or finishing their race too late, and the lone leader Rogue Empire, if reproducing recent winning form, has every chance of stealing a march on rivals who cannot all find clear daylight simultaneously. This race shape most benefits prominent trackers and horses with the resolution to grind out a finish in a strung-out single-file contest rather than those relying on a bunched late surge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rogue Empire Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Empire secures the lead unchallenged and sets a controlled, honest pace over two miles on fast ground.
scenarios.body: Owen Lewis (5) gives Rogue Empire a soft lead from the front, the field strings out behind him, and he has enough in reserve to repel late challenges having dictated every yard; his two recent wins over 2m on Good and Standard give him strong claims to replicate that form here.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Chargers Reel Him In
scenarios.trigger: If Rogue Empire's solo front-running drains him in the final quarter-mile and the hold-up horses close him down.
scenarios.body: A steady early pace gives the closers a relatively compact final sprint, and the horse with the sharpest finishing gear picks off the tiring leader close home; An Bradan Feasa's consistent placed form over 2m on Good ground makes him the likeliest beneficiary.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Horse Strikes Early
scenarios.trigger: If a redistributed midfield runner positions cleverly, travels into contention by the final turn, and wins with a sustained rather than explosive run.
scenarios.body: Laravie, who has won over 2m on Good and carries the visor as a focus aid, is well-suited to a single-file grinding contest where tactical position matters more than a late burst; her trainer's strong recent strike rate (9/45 in 14 days) adds confidence.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Compressed Finish, Outsider Lands
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and a tight, bunched finish opens the door for a lower-rated runner on the upgrade.
scenarios.body: The Craftymaster has won twice recently including over 2m on Good ground and carries the tongue-tie; if the race pans out in a wall of horses charging home together, his raw current form could be underestimated at the weights.

watchPoints.text: Rogue Empire is shown on the lead but is a natural hold-up horse — watch at the start to see whether Owen Lewis (5) actually commits to the front or allows another runner to take over, which would completely reshape the race dynamic.

An Bradan Feasa and Laravie are both genuine hold-up horses likely to race further back than the map shows; if they both sit last and the pace is slow, they risk a traffic-free but too-late finish — watch how Jake Dickson and Mason Paetel position them in the early furlongs.

Mio Amico returning from 94 days off is the key fitness risk in the race; watch his market move on the day and his early movement — if he is flat or sluggish in the first half-mile, he is unlikely to be competitive.

Free World carries the ⚠ fading-in-finish flag over 2m on Good to Firm — if the pace quickens materially in the final two furlongs, Ryan Kavanagh should ideally commit earlier than normal to avoid being swamped by horses with more resolution.

The Craftymaster's tongue-tie has coincided with his two recent wins; with the lowest OR in the field at 57, he is the most leniently weighted runner if reproducing that form and warrants monitoring in any market move before the off.
